title: Sustainable Agricultural Land Management
provider: University of Florida (via Coursera). Instructor: George J. Hochmuth, Ph.D.
language: Taught in English; subtitles/translation available in 22 languages (per Coursera page). Russian availability not individually confirmed [UNVERIFIED — page states "22 languages" without enumerating them].
cost: Audit/free access to course materials available; full course included with Coursera Plus subscription; a shareable certificate requires purchase. Free Trial and financial aid options offered. (Coursera page)
certificate: Yes — shareable electronic certificate added to the Coursera Accomplishments page; requires payment (not available on free audit).
duration: Approx. 2 weeks at ~10 hours/week as listed by Coursera (the original cohort design was 8 weeks, one module/lecture-set per week). 8 modules total, module workloads 2-4 hours each.
target_audience: Anyone interested in sustainable agriculture, water quality, and land management; framed for practitioners, farmers, and environmental/extension professionals — originally with a peer-assessed project tied to an agricultural/environmental issue "where the students live and work."
format: Self-paced online MOOC: ~3 video lectures per module, weekly quizzes, weekly discussion topics, and a multi-part peer-assessed course project. (Coursera + MOOC aggregator descriptions)
assessment: 8 quizzes (one per module, ~30 min each); 3 peer-reviewed course-project submissions (project parts span modules 2, 4, 6, with final submission in module 8); some AI-graded assignments noted on the current Coursera page.
hands_on: Practical work centers on a multi-part, peer-assessed Course Project in which learners analyze a real agricultural/environmental (water-quality/nutrient/land-management) issue relevant to their own region/work. No software lab or notebook component; project is analytical/written, built progressively across the modules.
tools: No specialized software, GIS, or coding tools required or mentioned. Content focuses conceptually on water-quality analysis, nutrient mass-balance reasoning, soil testing interpretation, and BMP evaluation. (Coursera page lists no tools.)

syllabus.module: Module 1 — Introduction to Sustainable Agricultural Land Management (~2 h)
syllabus.topics: Welcome and course overview; introduction to the instructor; introduction to the course project; three-part conceptual introduction to sustainable agricultural land management.

syllabus.module: Module 2 — Water Quality Issues and Regulations (~3 h)
syllabus.topics: Big-picture examples and the value of agriculture; overview of water quality and the regulatory landscape; Course Project Part 1.
TMDLs (Total Maximum Daily Loads) and agriculture; agricultural soils; nutrient fates (Part 1).
Nutrient fates (Parts 2-3); nutrient mass balance; Course Project Part 2.
Soil testing (Part 2); nutrient management (Parts 1-2); Course Project Part 3.
Nutrient management (Part 3); water resources in Florida; irrigation management (Part 1).
Irrigation management (Parts 2-3); overall course review; Course Project final submission.

strengths: High learner satisfaction: 4.8/5 from ~669 reviews, ~83% five-star, ~98% satisfaction, ~58k enrolled (Coursera page metrics).
Strong, coherent narrative thread: water quality -> regulation (TMDLs) -> nutrient fates -> BMPs -> soil/nutrient/irrigation management — a logical cause-to-practice arc.
Project-based learning grounded in the learner's OWN region/work, which reviewers said let them 'apply immediately to my work'.
Concrete pedagogy on nutrient mass balance and soil-test interpretation — reviewers cited nutrient management as the most valuable part.
Beginner-accessible, no prerequisites, free to audit — low barrier to entry.
Regulatory + scientific framing combined (policy behind BMPs), not just agronomy.
weaknesses: Heavily Florida-specific (Florida water bodies, Florida regulations, Florida irrigation context); a minority of reviewers found this limiting outside the region — direct relevance to North Kazakhstan dryland/rainfed systems is low without re-grounding.
Reviewers reported lectures can be 'dry and hard to follow at times' — talking-head video style.
Depth is uneven: praised as a solid introduction but criticized for lacking depth in specialized areas.
No software / quantitative tooling (no GIS, GEE, QGIS, Python) — purely conceptual, so it does not build technical/computational skills.

Water-quality and TMDL-regulatory emphasis is humid-subtropical and US-policy bound; assumes irrigation abundance rather than the moisture-limited, soil-degradation/salinization concerns dominant in СКО/Костанай/Акмола.
Certificate is paywalled; full project peer-review experience tied to paid/enrolled track.
borrow_for_folur: Adopt the single-spine narrative arc: проблема (качество воды/деградация почв) -> регуляторная рамка -> судьба питательных веществ/процессы -> лучшие практики (BMP) -> почвенный/питательный/водный менеджмент. Для FOLUR заменить флоридский водный фокус на доминирующие для СКО/Костанай/Акмола темы: деградация и засоление почв, влагосбережение, no-till/почвозащитное земледелие.

Borrow the 'project on YOUR own land/region' design: каждый слушатель (агро-МСБ) ведёт сквозной проект по своему реальному участку/хозяйству, сдаваемый по частям в модулях 2/4/6/8 — это даёт немедленную применимость, что прямо хвалили рецензенты.
Modular workload labeling (часы на модуль, 2-4 ч) — публиковать ожидаемую трудозатрату на каждый модуль для занятых практиков МСБ.
One quiz per module (~30 мин) + сквозной проект как двойной механизм оценки — лёгкая автопроверка знаний плюс прикладной артефакт; согласуется с автогрейдером и тест-движком платформы.

Teach an explicit, reusable analytical tool: nutrient mass balance / интерпретация почвенных анализов как переносимый навык — у FOLUR сделать аналогом расчёт баланса гумуса/N-P-K и чтение агрохимкартограмм по реальным региональным данным.

Connect science to local policy/regulation (как сделано с TMDL/BMP) — для FOLUR привязать практики к нормам РК и мерам субсидирования (помечать как [UNVERIFIED] до сверки с источниками, не выдумывать цифры субсидий).

AVOID copying their weaknesses: не делать «сухие» лекции — добавлять Mermaid-схемы, региональные кейсы и интерактив; обязательно включать $0-инструментарий (QGIS/GEE/Colab), которого у них нет, как практический дифференциатор FOLUR.
